doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Writing the Sheraton 800-number jingle overnight
summary: Jim Jordan of BBDO asked for a jingle for a phone number; she wrote it on the drive in.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: just briefly take me from when you first get contacted to do a product and the sequence of events that ends up with a commercial?
Can I tell you two interesting stories?

Okay the first one is at 5:30 Jim Jordan, who was then the president of BBD and O but he had been a copywriter, the first copywriter to rise to the presidency. And I was doing a lot of stuff for him. And it was about 5:30 at night and I’m making dinner for the kids. And he says, “Anne, listen, the Sheraton account is in Boston but they haven’t been able to do this. It’s a telephone number and can you come in tomorrow at 8:30?” And so it was, he said, “They’re switching to the 800 number, so the number is 800-325-3535. And I said, “Well can we do it like 8-oh-oh instead? And he said, “Yeah, either way it’s all right.” And so at 8:00 the next morning I was driving into New York to go to BBDO and standing there was the entire account people behind me and I’m at the piano doing, [sings] 8-oh-oh-325-3535, which lasted longer than the 13-week promo for the new telephone number.
Were you singing that in your head on the way?
I wrote it on the way in, because everything I wrote the night before was awful.
Oh that’s so interesting. Wow. You had to go through the process. The deadline loomed.
